findings.finding: The shot starts with the performer small and full-length beneath a dominant mirror ball, rather than in the planned thighs-up performance frame. It travels through a substantial scale change and reaches the intended framing only at the close, making the room reveal more prominent than his delivery.
findings.fix: Regenerate or replace with a thighs-up performance setup from the opening, using a locked camera or restrained push. Preserve the lighting change at 1.9 seconds, but keep the mirror ball secondary to his face and gestures.

findings.finding: The moving sneaker appears empty and disconnected from a leg in the opening and middle frames. It floats beside a second, planted shoe, then a trouser leg becomes visible near the close; this does not read as a continuous, weight-bearing step onto the runway.
findings.fix: Replace the insert with a low, tight shot of white sneakers worn on clearly connected lower legs. Show one simple heel-to-toe step beside the light strip, maintaining ankle continuity, floor contact and a matching reflection throughout the 3.9 seconds.

findings.finding: The performer remains full-length throughout instead of thighs-up. The centered wide-to-nearer push repeats shot 39’s composition, including the large overhead mirror ball, rather than returning to a fresh, performance-led frame.
findings.fix: Swap or regenerate this shot as a locked thighs-up performance against the dark back wall. Keep the hard pool, but exclude most or all of the mirror ball so the return from the sneaker insert gives his delivery renewed emphasis.

findings.finding: After the scheduled blackout, the performer becomes a silhouette, but both runway strips remain illuminated and a brilliant mirror ball throws dense points and visible rays across the room. No sharp jewelry highlights establish his ice as the source, so the hook’s defining visual promise is missing.
findings.fix: Rebuild the post-4.7-second lighting state: extinguish the pool and runway strips, suppress the mirror ball’s luminous globe and radiating beams, and leave sparse, sharp glints visibly associated with his ice, carrying reflections onto the gloss floor and camouflage. Preserve his position and performance through the cue.

astra_review.release: Not ready to release. Replace shot 40’s disconnected sneaker motion, tighten the performance framing in shots 39 and 41, and rebuild shot 42’s blackout so the artist’s ice—not the runway strips and glowing mirror ball—provides the visual payoff.
strengths: The vertical frames maintain a coherent black-runway world, with empty seating, glossy flooring and strong white perspective lines.
The camouflage shirt, flag patch, navy cap, glasses and beard remain broadly consistent across the performance shots.
Both scheduled lighting changes are visible: shot 39 introduces mirror-ball reflections, and shot 42 drops the hard pool and darkens the performer.
astra_review.summary: The runway world holds together, but the mirror ball commands more attention than the artist. The sneaker insert breaks physical credibility, and the repeated wide performance setups weaken the section’s momentum. The final lighting cue happens, but it delivers a brightly illuminated disco room rather than the promised ice-only blackout. Mouth-to-song synchronization cannot be verified from these frames.

treatment_json_before.concept:
YSL — “INTERRUPTED BROADCAST”
Proposed music-video treatment

An impossible Saint Laurent–inspired fashion show takes over Fendi’s television, then spills into his Chicago surroundings. Fire becomes snow. A luxury SUV contains a television control room. Every new location seems to be broadcasting the next—and Fendi remains composed as the world around him becomes increasingly extraordinary.

Opening — The burning show

We begin high above a forest at night. At first, it reads as aerial footage of a wildfire: smoke obscures sections of the ground, flames crawl along the tree line, and wind pushes embers across the darkness.

As the camera advances, a deliberate shape emerges. An enormous YSL monogram has been cut into the forest floor. Fire surrounds its perimeter; inside its cleared strokes, models move in intersecting formations.

From above, their movement appears disciplined. At ground level, it feels like organized chaos: models pass close to the lens, cross behind one another, and disappear into drifting smoke. No audience. No conventional runway. Everyone behaves as though this extraordinary location is completely normal.

The clothes receive proper fashion coverage: a compressed telephoto view of silhouettes through heat shimmer; a low tracking shot following boots through ash; a close view of leather catching firelight. These are specific garments with weight, construction, and texture.

Among the walking models, one beautiful Black woman approaches a horse. We see her hand settle against its neck, a boot enter the stirrup, and her weight shift into the saddle. She rides along the cleared route between walls of fire. The cuts alternate between her controlled movement and the models’ intersecting paths.

A side-on shot of the rider suddenly loses its color.

The viewer

We pull back from that same image playing on a small black-and-white CRT television.

Fendi sits in his exact YSL denim look, watching. The room is spare and tangible: worn upholstery, television glass reflecting a lamp, cables disappearing behind the set. The fashion show feels like a strange transmission he has found late at night.

The rider turns toward the broadcast camera.

The television snaps to a white point. Every light in the room dies.

A close-up reveals another woman’s hand at a wall switch. She flips it.

Chicago — The switch

The click lands with the vocal entrance.

Light returns, but the room is gone. Fendi occupies the same position in the frame, now standing at 79th and Lafayette by the Red Line, wearing his exact YSL leather coat.

The woman completes her movement beside him. An illuminated storefront or practical fixture motivates the returning light. Passing traffic, the station environment, and people moving through the background establish a recognizable Chicago street.

Fendi performs directly to camera. We stay with him long enough for his presence and delivery to own the scene.

On “you don’t gotta cut the lights on, this ice on,” we move into an extreme close-up of his mouth. Diamond-set sections of the grill rotate like miniature mechanical reels, catching available streetlight before locking into alignment.

The lips, gums, and surrounding teeth remain stable. No glowing mouth, floating jewels, or cartoon symbols. The effect lasts just long enough to register, then resolves into the intact grill.

The cold front

A bright reflection off the final diamond becomes a whiteout.

A passing veil of snow reveals Fendi in his specified YSL jacket, performing in a blizzard. Wind moves the garment and drives snow consistently across the frame. His breath catches in the cold.

A polar bear crosses behind him with a heavy chain settling into its fur. Elsewhere, penguins move through the foreground, their smaller jewelry partially disappearing beneath feathers.

The animals behave like animals: uneven steps, shifting weight, incidental glances. Their indifference makes the surreal styling more convincing. Fendi remains the center of the performance.

The camera crew

On “more cameras in the whip than a camera crew,” we cut inside a cramped mobile broadcast control room.

Monitors show Fendi performing in Chicago and the blizzard. One carries the burning fashion show. Crew members adjust equipment while he raps across the screens.

A camera operator shoulders a camera and reaches for the exit. We follow toward the opening door—

—and cut outside to reveal a Maybach SUV.

The operator steps down from its passenger compartment. More crew members follow with full-size news cameras. The exterior shot holds long enough to let the impossible interior register without explaining it.

On “all this ice around me, need a Canada Goose,” the crew abruptly has to yield to geese crossing their path in miniature Canada Goose jackets. One goose pauses, forcing an impatient operator to stop.

It plays as a brief, deadpan interruption. Nobody performs the joke for the audience.

The clean entrance

A news camera swings toward a nearby building. We cut into its view.

On “so clean, but I don’t do what the janitors do,” impeccably dressed models approach the entrance. A janitor is finishing the floor beside a yellow wet-floor sign.

Their movement recalls the formations inside the burning monogram. The camera drops toward the freshly cleaned surface, where shoes and garment silhouettes reflect sharply.

Fendi passes the camera and enters with them. The janitor pulls the caution sign aside just before his step.

Inside, a security monitor shows the woman on horseback.

She is arriving at this building.

The broadcast is now ahead of reality.

sections.intent: Cut the lights so the diamond mirror ball alone illuminates him, turning jewelry into the only moving light source.

sections.intent: Answer each lyric with runway, fitting-room and night-street details while returning to varied performance frames.
